ru: собирать вещи, собрать вещи; сворачиваться, свернуться
separable: separable — *pack up your tools*, and *pack them up*; it also works with no object at all: *we packed up and left*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*pack up the dishes*), intransitive (*we packed up and drove home*)
gloss: To put your things into bags or boxes, usually in order to finish and leave.
examples: We *packed up* the campsite before sunrise.
She *packs up* her laptop the moment the meeting ends.
They're *packing up* the office this weekend.

ru: убирать, убрать (на хранение); складывать, сложить
separable: separable — *pack away the tent*, and *pack it away*.
gloss: To put something into storage until it is needed again.
examples: He *packed away* the Christmas lights in January.
*Pack* the good china *away* before the kids get home.
The winter coats have been *packed away* since April.

ru: набирать, набрать (вес, мышечную массу)
separable: separable — *pack on ten pounds*, and with a pronoun *pack it on*.
gloss: To gain weight or muscle, usually quickly.
examples: He *packed on* twenty pounds his first year of college.
She's *packing on* muscle after three months of lifting.
Those late-night snacks *pack on* the pounds.

ru: отправлять, отправить (кого-л. куда-л.); спроваживать, спровадить
separable: separable — *pack off the kids*, and with a pronoun the split is required: *packed him off*, never *packed off him*.
gloss: To send someone away to another place, often without asking them first.
examples: His parents *packed him off* to summer camp.
They *pack* the boys *off* to their grandmother's every July.
She was *packed off* to boarding school at twelve.

ru: заканчивать, закончить (на сегодня); бросать, бросить (дело)
separable: separable, and in practice the object is almost always *it*: *pack it in*.
gloss: To stop doing something and call it a day.
examples: After ten hours of driving we *packed it in* and found a motel.
The band *packed it in* after twenty years on the road.
It's almost midnight — let's *pack it in*.
contrast: The pronoun always splits it: *pack it in*, never *pack in it*.

ru: закрашивать, закрасить; замазывать краской, замазать
separable: separable — *paint over the marks*, and *paint them over*.
gloss: To hide something by putting a new layer of paint on top of it.
examples: The landlord just *painted over* the water stain.
They *paint over* the graffiti every Monday.
You can't fix rust by *painting over* it.

ru: объединяться в пары, объединиться; разбивать на пары, разбить
separable: separable when it has an object — *pair up the students*, *pair them up*; with no object it stands alone: *we paired up*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*the teacher paired us up*), intransitive (*we paired up for the drill*)
gloss: To join with another person to form a pair, or to put two people together.
examples: The teacher *paired up* the new students with volunteers.
We *pair up* for the drills every practice.
They're *pairing up* to run the relay.

ru: разбиваться на пары, разбиться на пары; расходиться парами
separable: usually intransitive and unsplit — *the guests paired off*; when it does take an object it separates: *pair them off*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*the guests paired off*), transitive (*the coach paired them off*)
gloss: To divide into pairs, especially into couples.
examples: By the end of the trip everyone had *paired off*.
The dancers *pair off* as soon as the music starts.
Guests were *pairing off* for the last dance.

ru: всучивать, всучить; сбывать, сбыть (подделку, негодное)
separable: separable — *palm off the broken one*, and *palm it off*; the person tricked follows *on*: *palmed it off on me*.
gloss: To get rid of something worthless by tricking someone into taking it.
examples: The dealer *palmed off* a fake watch on a tourist.
Don't let him *palm* his old laptop *off* on you.
She's been *palming off* her weekend shifts on the new guy.

ru: получаться, получиться; выгорать, выгореть (о планах)
separable: intransitive — it takes no object, so nothing can split it: *the plan didn't pan out*.
gloss: To turn out the way someone hoped; to succeed.
examples: The job in Denver never *panned out*.
Let's see how the first week *pans out*.
Nothing was *panning out*, so he moved back home.
contrast: *panned*, *panning* — the single *n* doubles before *-ed* and *-ing*.

ru: замазывать, замазать (разногласия); сглаживать, сгладить; прикрывать, прикрыть
separable: separable — *paper over the differences*, and *paper them over*.
gloss: To hide a problem or a disagreement instead of dealing with it.
examples: The statement *papered over* a serious split in the party.
They keep *papering over* the same complaints.
You can't *paper over* a broken process with a nicer dashboard.

ru: сокращать, сократить; урезать (список, бюджет)
separable: separable — *pare down the list*, and *pare it down*.
gloss: To reduce something by cutting parts of it away.
examples: We *pared down* the guest list to forty.
The company *pares down* its catalog every fall.
They're *paring* the budget *down* to the essentials.
contrast: The *-e* drops before *-ing*: *paring*, not *pareing*.

ru: расставаться, расстаться (с чем-л.); отдавать, отдать
separable: inseparable — *part with the money*, and *part with it*; never *part it with*.
gloss: To give up something that you would rather keep.
examples: He finally *parted with* his father's truck.
She *parts with* nothing — the garage is full.
I'm not *parting with* that guitar for any price.

ru: умирать, умереть; уходить из жизни, уйти из жизни
separable: intransitive — it takes no object: *she passed away in her sleep*.
gloss: To die — the gentle way of saying it.
examples: Her grandfather *passed away* last spring.
Both of his parents have *passed away*.
We say someone *passes away* when *died* feels too blunt.
contrast: Third person is *passes away* — a verb ending in *-ss* adds *-es*.

ru: терять сознание, потерять сознание; падать в обморок, упасть
separable: intransitive — no object, so nothing can split it: *he passed out*.
gloss: To lose consciousness suddenly.
examples: He *passed out* at the sight of the needle.
She almost *passes out* every time she gives blood.
Two runners were *passing out* in the heat.
contrast: The same two words also mean to hand things out, but that sense takes an object: *passed out the forms*. Fainting never does.

ru: раздавать, раздать
separable: separable — *pass out the flyers*, and *pass them out*.
gloss: To give one of something to each person in a group.
examples: The teacher *passed out* the tests.
Volunteers *pass out* water at mile eight.
He's *passing* the programs *out* at the door.

ru: упускать, упустить (возможность); отказываться, отказаться от
separable: separable — *pass up the offer*, and *pass it up*.
gloss: To decide not to take a chance or an offer.
examples: She *passed up* a job in Chicago to stay near family.
You don't *pass up* free tickets.
He's *passing up* the chance to go first.

ru: отказываться, отказаться (от предложенного); пропускать, пропустить
separable: inseparable — what you refuse follows *on*: *pass on dessert*, *pass on it*. In this meaning *pass it on* is wrong.
gloss: To politely refuse something that is offered.
examples: I'll *pass on* dessert, thanks.
She *passed on* the invitation and stayed home.
They're *passing on* the deal for now.
contrast: *Pass on the cake* means refuse it. *Pass the cake on* means hand it to the next person.

ru: передавать, передать (дальше, другому)
separable: separable — *pass on the news*, *pass the news on*, and *pass it on*.
gloss: To give something to the next person, or to hand knowledge on to someone else.
examples: *Pass* the message *on* to your manager.
He *passed on* everything his father taught him.
The recipe has been *passed on* for four generations.

ru: скончаться; уходить из жизни, уйти из жизни
separable: intransitive — it takes no object: *he passed on last year*.
gloss: To die — a soft, slightly old-fashioned way of saying it.
examples: Her husband *passed on* two winters ago.
Both grandparents had *passed on* before she was born.
When someone *passes on*, the family often puts it that way.

ru: передавать, передать (информацию, просьбу дальше)
separable: separable — *pass along the message*, *pass the message along*, and *pass it along*.
gloss: To give information or something you were given to the person it should reach next.
examples: I *passed along* your question to the engineers.
She *passes along* every article she likes.
Thanks — I'll *pass* that *along*.

ru: передавать, передать (по наследству, из поколения в поколение)
separable: separable — *pass down the farm*, and *pass it down*; very often passive: *it was passed down*.
gloss: To give something to a younger generation of the family.
examples: The watch was *passed down* from his grandfather.
They *pass down* the same stories every Thanksgiving.
She's *passing* the business *down* to her daughter.

ru: выдавать за, выдать за
separable: separable — the thing goes in the middle: *pass it off as new*; what it is pretended to be follows *as*.
gloss: To make something or someone seem to be what they are not.
examples: He tried to *pass off* a copy *as* the original.
She *passed* herself *off as* a reporter.
They're *passing* cheap steel *off as* stainless.

ru: сходить за, сойти за
separable: inseparable — *pass for a local*, and *pass for one*; never *pass one for*.
gloss: To be accepted as something or someone you are not.
examples: He could easily *pass for* thirty.
That sauce *passed for* homemade at the potluck.
In this light it's *passing for* leather.

ru: обходить, обойти (при повышении); игнорировать, проигнорировать
separable: separable — *pass over the obvious choice*, and with a pronoun the split is required: *passed him over*.
gloss: To ignore someone when deciding who gets a job or a promotion.
examples: They *passed* her *over* for the manager job.
He has been *passed over* twice now.
The committee *passes over* anyone without field experience.

ru: проходить мимо, пройти мимо (о жизни, возможности)
separable: separable when it has an object — *life passed him by*, *don't let it pass you by*; with no object it stands alone: *the years passed by*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*the chance passed her by*), intransitive (*two summers passed by*)
gloss: To go past someone without involving them, so that they miss out on it.
examples: He felt life was *passing him by*.
Another chance *passed by* while she waited.
Don't let the offer *pass* you *by*.

ru: пускать по кругу, пустить по кругу; передавать друг другу
separable: separable — *pass around the cookies*, and *pass them around*.
gloss: To give something to one person after another until everyone in the group has seen or taken it.
examples: She *passed around* a sign-up sheet.
*Pass* the photos *around* so everyone can see.
They're *passing around* a card for him to sign.

ru: латать, залатать; чинить наспех, починить
separable: separable — *patch up the roof*, and *patch it up*.
gloss: To repair something quickly and roughly so that it will hold for now.
examples: The mechanic *patched up* the radiator well enough to get us home.
He *patches up* the same fence every spring.
Medics were *patching up* players on the sideline.
contrast: Third person is *patches up* — verbs ending in *-ch* add *-es*.

ru: улаживать, уладить (ссору); мириться, помириться
separable: separable, and the object is often *things*: *patch things up*, *patch up their differences*.
gloss: To settle a quarrel and make a relationship good again.
examples: They *patched things up* after a month of silence.
She's trying to *patch up* her friendship with her sister.
The two sides have *patched up* their differences.

ru: соединять, соединить (по телефону); переключать, переключить
separable: separable — *patch the call through*, and with a pronoun the split is required: *patch me through*.
gloss: To connect a phone call to another person or place.
examples: The operator *patched* me *through* to dispatch.
Can you *patch* this call *through* to her cell?
We're *patching* you *through* now.

ru: отклеиваться, отклеиться; облезать, облезть; отдирать, отодрать
separable: separable when it has an object — *peel off the label*, *peel it off*; with no object it stands alone: *the paint peeled off*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*peel off the sticker*), intransitive (*the paint peeled off*)
gloss: To come away from a surface in a layer, or to pull such a layer away.
examples: The paint is *peeling off* the porch railing.
She *peeled off* the price tag before wrapping it.
The old decal *peels off* easily with a hair dryer.

ru: срываться с места, сорваться с места (на машине, с визгом шин)
separable: intransitive — no object: *the truck peeled out*.
gloss: To drive away very fast, with the tires squealing.
examples: He *peeled out* of the parking lot.
Kids *peel out* at that light every night.
Someone was *peeling out* behind the gym at two in the morning.
contrast: Not the same as *peel off*: *peel out* is only about a vehicle leaving fast.

ru: предварительно записывать, записать; намечать, наметить (встречу)
separable: separable — *pencil in a meeting*, and with a pronoun the split is required: *pencil me in*.
gloss: To put something on the schedule for now, knowing it may still change.
examples: I've *penciled you in* for Thursday at ten.
Let's *pencil in* lunch next week.
They're *penciling in* a launch date for spring.
contrast: American spelling keeps one *l*: *penciled*, *penciling*. British English doubles it: *pencilled*.

ru: оживлять, оживить; взбадривать, взбодрить
separable: separable — *pep up the presentation*, and *pep it up*.
gloss: To make someone or something more lively or more interesting.
examples: A little chili *peps up* the soup.
The coffee *pepped* him *up* for the drive.
They're *pepping up* the intro with music.
contrast: *pepped*, *pepping* — the final *p* doubles.

ru: оживляться, оживиться; взбадриваться, взбодриться; подбадривать, подбодрить
separable: separable when it has an object — *perk up the room*, *perk him up*; with no object it stands alone: *he perked up*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*she perked up*), transitive (*the news perked us up*)
gloss: To become more cheerful or more lively, or to make someone feel that way.
examples: She *perked up* as soon as the dog came in.
A nap usually *perks* him *up*.
The whole class was *perking up* by the end of the hour.

ru: иссякать, иссякнуть; сходить на нет, сойти на нет
separable: intransitive — no object: *the money petered out*.
gloss: To fade away slowly until there is nothing left.
examples: The trail *petered out* two miles in.
Interest in the project *peters out* every winter.
Their conversation was *petering out*.

ru: постепенно сворачивать, свернуть; постепенно отказываться от, отказаться от
separable: separable — *phase out the program*, and *phase it out*.
gloss: To stop using or producing something gradually, in stages.
examples: The company *phased out* the old model last year.
They *phase out* summer hours in September.
Coal plants are being *phased out* across the state.

ru: постепенно вводить, ввести; поэтапно внедрять, внедрить
separable: separable — *phase in the changes*, and *phase them in*.
gloss: To introduce something gradually, a part at a time.
examples: The city *phased in* the new fares over six months.
We *phase in* each feature after testing it.
The rules are being *phased in* district by district.

ru: звонить, позвонить (сообщить или заказать по телефону)
separable: separable when it has an object — *phone in the order*, *phone it in*; with no object it stands alone: *he phoned in sick*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*phone in an order*), intransitive (*she phoned in this morning*)
gloss: To telephone a place with a report, an order, or a message.
examples: She *phoned in* sick on Monday.
Listeners *phone in* their requests all morning.
He's *phoning in* the order now.

ru: делать спустя рукава, сделать спустя рукава; халтурить, схалтурить
separable: the object is fixed — always *phone it in*, never *phone in it*.
gloss: To do something with the least effort possible, without really trying.
examples: The band clearly *phoned it in* on the second night.
He *phones it in* every Friday afternoon.
You can tell she's *phoning it in* lately.
contrast: Different from *phone in* (to call something in to an office). *Phone it in* is about effort, and always keeps *it*.

ru: поднимать, поднять (с пола, со стола); брать в руки
separable: separable — *pick up the box*, and with a pronoun the split is required: *pick it up*, never *pick up it*.
gloss: To take hold of something and lift it from a surface.
examples: He *picked up* the pen and signed.
*Pick* your socks *up* off the floor.
She's *picking up* the pieces of the broken mug.

ru: забирать, забрать; заезжать за, заехать за
separable: separable — *pick up the kids*, and with a pronoun the split is required: *pick them up*.
gloss: To collect someone or something from a place, usually in a car.
examples: I'll *pick you up* at seven.
She *picked up* the dry cleaning on the way home.
He's *picking up* his sister from the airport.

ru: осваивать, освоить (мимоходом); нахвататься; подхватывать, подхватить (навык, язык)
separable: separable — *pick up a language*, and *pick it up*.
gloss: To learn something casually, without formally studying it.
examples: He *picked up* Spanish working summers in Texas.
Kids *pick up* accents fast.
She's *picking up* the software as she goes.

ru: покупать, купить (по дороге); брать, взять (заодно)
separable: separable — *pick up some bread*, and *pick it up*.
gloss: To buy something while you are out, usually something small.
examples: Can you *pick up* milk on your way home?
He *picked up* a phone charger at the airport.
We're *picking up* dinner on the way.

ru: оживляться, оживиться; налаживаться, наладиться; усиливаться, усилиться
separable: intransitive in this meaning — nothing follows it: *business picked up*.
gloss: To improve or become busier after a slow period.
examples: Business always *picks up* in December.
Sales *picked up* after the ad ran.
The wind is *picking up*.

ru: набирать, набрать (скорость, обороты)
separable: separable in form — *pick up speed*, *pick it up* — but the object here is nearly always a noun like *speed*, *steam* or *momentum*.
gloss: To gain more of something, especially speed or momentum.
examples: The train *picked up* speed on the straightaway.
The campaign is *picking up* momentum.
He *picks up* steam in the second half of every race.

ru: брать трубку, взять трубку; отвечать на звонок, ответить
separable: usually intransitive — *nobody picked up*; with an object it separates: *pick up the phone*, *pick it up*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*nobody picked up*), transitive (*pick up the phone*)
gloss: To answer a ringing telephone.
examples: Nobody *picked up*.
She *picks up* on the first ring.
He kept calling, and no one was *picking up*.

ru: прибирать, прибрать; убирать, убрать (в комнате)
separable: separable — *pick up the room*, and *pick it up*; it also works with no object: *pick up after yourself*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*pick up the toys*), intransitive (*everyone picks up before we close*)
gloss: To tidy a room or space by putting things back where they belong.
examples: *Pick up* your room before dinner.
He *picked up* the living room in ten minutes.
The kids are *picking up* the playroom now.

ru: подхватывать, подхватить (болезнь); заражаться, заразиться
separable: separable — *pick up a virus*, and *pick it up*.
gloss: To catch an illness or an infection.
examples: She *picked up* a cold on the flight.
Kids *pick up* everything at daycare.
He's *picking up* every bug going around the office.

ru: задерживать, задержать (о полиции); забирать, забрать (в участок)
separable: separable — *pick up the suspect*, and with a pronoun the split is required: *pick him up*.
gloss: To stop someone and take them into police custody.
examples: Police *picked him up* two blocks away.
He was *picked up* on an old warrant.
They *pick up* the same guy every summer.

ru: продолжать, продолжить (с того места, где остановились); возобновлять, возобновить
separable: separable when it has an object — *pick up the discussion*, *pick it up*; often used with none: *let's pick up where we stopped*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*we picked up after lunch*), transitive (*they picked the story up again*)
gloss: To start again from the point where something stopped.
examples: Let's *pick up* where we left off.
The second season *picks up* ten years later.
They *picked up* the conversation after lunch.

ru: замечать, заметить; улавливать, уловить (намёк, настроение)
separable: inseparable — the object follows *on*: *pick up on the hint*, *pick up on it*; never *pick it up on*.
gloss: To notice something that was not said directly.
examples: She *picked up on* the tension right away.
He never *picks up on* hints.
I'm *picking up on* something in his tone.
contrast: *Pick up on* is about noticing. Plain *pick up* is about collecting or learning.

ru: убирать за, убрать за (кем-л.)
separable: inseparable — the person follows *after*: *pick up after the kids*, *pick up after them*.
gloss: To clean up the mess that someone else has left.
examples: I'm tired of *picking up after* my roommate.
She *picked up after* the whole crew.
Nobody *picks up after* themselves in that office.

ru: выбирать, выбрать; подбирать, подобрать
separable: separable — *pick out a shirt*, and *pick it out*.
gloss: To choose one thing from among several.
examples: She *picked out* a blue one.
He *picks out* his tie the night before.
We're *picking out* paint colors this weekend.

ru: различать, различить; высматривать, высмотреть (в толпе)
separable: separable — *pick out one face*, and with a pronoun the split is required: *pick her out*.
gloss: To see or hear one thing clearly among many others.
examples: I could *pick* her voice *out* in the crowd.
He *picked out* his brother in the team photo.
You can just *pick out* the coastline through the fog.

ru: придираться к, придраться к; травить, задирать
separable: inseparable — *pick on the new kid*, *pick on him*; never *pick him on*.
gloss: To treat one person unfairly, teasing or criticizing them again and again.
examples: The older boys *picked on* him all year.
She feels the manager *picks on* her.
Stop *picking on* your brother.

ru: ковыряться в тарелке, ковырять (еду); есть без аппетита
separable: inseparable — *pick at your food*, *pick at it*; never *pick it at*.
gloss: To eat only small bits of a meal, with no appetite.
examples: He *picked at* his dinner and left most of it.
She *picks at* her food when she's nervous.
The kids were *picking at* the salad.

ru: разбирать по косточкам, разобрать по косточкам; раскритиковать
separable: separable — *pick apart the theory*, and *pick it apart*.
gloss: To criticize something in detail, finding fault with every part of it.
examples: The reviewers *picked apart* his argument.
She *picks apart* every draft I send.
They're *picking* the proposal *apart* line by line.

ru: отстреливать, отстрелить (по одному); выбивать, выбить поодиночке
separable: separable — *pick off the stragglers*, and *pick them off*.
gloss: To shoot or remove people or things one at a time.
examples: Snipers *picked off* the streetlights one by one.
That firm *picks off* our best engineers every year.
Hawks were *picking off* the chicks.

ru: собирать воедино, собрать воедино; восстанавливать, восстановить (картину событий)
separable: separable — *piece together the story*, and *piece it together*.
gloss: To build an understanding of something out of separate small pieces of information.
examples: Investigators *pieced together* the last hour of the flight.
She *pieces together* the family history from old letters.
We're *piecing together* what happened.
contrast: The *-e* drops before *-ing*: *piecing*, not *pieceing*.

ru: объедаться, объесться; обжираться, обожраться
separable: intransitive — no object; what you eat follows *on*: *pig out on ice cream*.
gloss: To eat a very large amount of food at one time.
examples: We *pigged out* on pizza after the game.
He *pigs out* every Thanksgiving.
They were *pigging out* in front of the TV.
contrast: *pigged*, *pigging* — the final *g* doubles.

ru: накапливаться, накопиться; скапливаться, скопиться; наваливать, навалить
separable: separable when it has an object — *pile up the logs*, *pile them up*; most often intransitive: *the work piled up*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*the mail piled up*), transitive (*he piled up the boxes*)
gloss: To grow into a large amount, usually one nobody wanted.
examples: The dishes *piled up* all week.
Bills *pile up* fast when you're out sick.
Snow was *piling up* against the door.

ru: наваливать, навалить (ещё); усиливать, усилить (давление, критику)
separable: separable when it has an object — *pile on the pressure*, *pile it on*; also used alone: *everyone piled on*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*they piled on more work*), intransitive (*the commentators piled on*)
gloss: To add even more of something, or to join everyone else in criticizing someone.
examples: The commentators *piled on* after the fumble.
Management keeps *piling on* more work.
Once one person complains, everybody *piles on*.

ru: набиваться в, набиться в; залезать всей гурьбой, залезть
separable: inseparable — *pile into the car*, *pile into it*.
gloss: To get into a vehicle or a room in a crowd, all at once.
examples: Six of us *piled into* the back of the van.
The team *piles into* the diner after every game.
They were *piling into* the elevator as I left.

ru: припирать к стенке, припереть к стенке (добиваясь конкретики); точно определять, определить
separable: separable — *pin down the date*, and with a pronoun the split is required: *pin him down*.
gloss: To make someone give a definite answer, or to work out exactly what something is.
examples: I couldn't *pin* him *down* on a date.
The doctors finally *pinned down* the cause.
She's still *pinning down* the details.
contrast: *pinned*, *pinning* — the final *n* doubles.

ru: сваливать вину на, свалить вину на; вешать на, повесить на
separable: separable — the thing blamed goes first, the person after *on*: *pin it on him*, *pin the delay on the weather*.
gloss: To blame someone for something, often unfairly.
examples: They *pinned* the whole mess *on* the intern.
He *pins* every delay *on* the weather.
The blame was *pinned on* her because she signed it.

ru: подавать голос, подать голос; вставлять слово, вставить
separable: intransitive — no object: *a kid piped up*.
gloss: To speak suddenly, often when nobody expected you to.
examples: A kid in the back *piped up* with the right answer.
She *pipes up* whenever the numbers come out wrong.
Someone was *piping up* from the hallway.

ru: замолкать, замолкнуть; успокаиваться, успокоиться (потише!)
separable: intransitive — no object: *everybody piped down*.
gloss: To stop talking or making noise.
examples: *Pipe down* — I'm on the phone.
The crowd *piped down* when the lights went out.
She *pipes down* the second her father walks in.

ru: включаться в работу, включиться; вносить свой вклад, внести; скидываться, скинуться
separable: usually intransitive — *everyone pitched in*; an amount can follow directly: *pitch in twenty dollars*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*they all pitched in*), transitive (*each of us pitched in ten dollars*)
gloss: To join in and help with a job that everyone shares.
examples: Everyone *pitched in* and the kitchen was clean in ten minutes.
Neighbors *pitch in* when someone's walk needs shoveling.
We're all *pitching in* for her gift.
contrast: Third person is *pitches in* — verbs ending in *-ch* add *-es*.

ru: продумывать, продумать; распланировать, планировать в деталях
separable: separable — *plan out the trip*, and *plan it out*.
gloss: To work out all the details of something in advance.
examples: We *planned out* the whole route the night before.
She *plans out* her week every Sunday.
They're *planning out* the renovation room by room.
contrast: *planned*, *planning* — the final *n* doubles.

ru: подыгрывать, подыграть; делать вид, что согласен
separable: intransitive — no object; the person you humor follows *with*: *play along with him*.
gloss: To pretend to agree or cooperate, to avoid trouble or to keep a joke going.
examples: He knew it was a prank but *played along*.
Just *play along* until she opens the gift.
She's been *playing along* with their story all week.

ru: валять дурака, дурачиться; бездельничать
separable: intransitive — no object: *stop playing around*.
gloss: To waste time being silly instead of doing what you should.
examples: Quit *playing around* and finish your homework.
They *played around* for an hour and got nothing done.
He *plays around* all week and panics on Friday.

ru: экспериментировать с, поэкспериментировать; возиться с, повозиться
separable: inseparable — the object follows *with*: *play around with the settings*, *play around with them*.
gloss: To try something out in a casual way, to see what it can do.
examples: I *played around with* the settings until it looked right.
She *plays around with* recipes on weekends.
We're *playing around with* a few designs.

ru: воспроизводить, воспроизвести (запись); прослушивать заново, прослушать
separable: separable — *play back the tape*, and *play it back*.
gloss: To play a recording again so that you can hear or watch it.
examples: *Play* the last ten seconds *back*.
They *played back* the security video frame by frame.
He's *playing back* the interview to check a quote.

ru: преуменьшать, преуменьшить; принижать значение, принизить
separable: separable — *play down the risk*, and *play it down*.
gloss: To make something seem less important or less serious than it is.
examples: The coach *played down* the injury.
She *plays down* her part in the win.
They're *playing down* the cost.

ru: подчёркивать, подчеркнуть; выпячивать, выпятить (достоинства)
separable: separable — *play up the discount*, and *play it up*.
gloss: To give something extra attention so that it seems more important or more attractive.
examples: The ad *plays up* the free shipping.
He *played up* his years in the field.
They're *playing up* the local angle.
contrast: In British English *play up* also means to misbehave or to malfunction. In American English the emphasizing sense is the usual one.

ru: разворачиваться, развернуться (о событиях); складываться, сложиться
separable: intransitive — no object: *we'll see how it plays out*.
gloss: To happen and develop to the end, in a way people can watch.
examples: Let's see how the season *plays out*.
The argument *played out* in front of everyone.
The same pattern is *playing out* in other cities.

ru: играть на (чувствах), сыграть на; пользоваться, воспользоваться (слабостью)
separable: inseparable — the feeling follows *on*: *play on their fears*, *play on it*.
gloss: To take advantage of someone's feelings or weakness.
examples: The ad *plays on* parents' fears.
He *played on* her sympathy to borrow the car.
They're *playing on* our impatience.

ru: продираться через, продраться; осиливать, осилить (большой объём)
separable: inseparable — the object follows *through*: *plow through the reading*, *plow through it*.
gloss: To work your way through something long or tedious until it is finished.
examples: I *plowed through* three hundred pages last night.
She *plows through* the inbox first thing every morning.
We're still *plowing through* the applications.
contrast: American spelling is *plow*; British English writes *plough*.

ru: врезаться в, врезаться (на большой скорости)
separable: inseparable — *plow into the fence*, *plow into it*.
gloss: To crash into something with great force.
examples: A truck *plowed into* the guardrail.
He *plowed into* a parked car backing out of the driveway.
Waves were *plowing into* the seawall.

ru: включать в розетку, включить; подключать, подключить
separable: separable — *plug in the toaster*, and with a pronoun the split is required: *plug it in*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*plug in the charger*), intransitive (*the speaker plugs in here*)
gloss: To connect a device to an electrical outlet.
examples: Did you *plug* the router back *in*?
She *plugged in* the lamp and nothing happened.
It charges whenever it's *plugged in*.
contrast: *plugged*, *plugging* — the final *g* doubles.

ru: упорно работать, корпеть (над чем-л.); не сдаваться
separable: intransitive — no object; the task follows *at*: *plug away at the report*.
gloss: To keep working steadily at something slow or difficult.
examples: He *plugged away* at the dissertation for six years.
She *plugs away* at it an hour every night.
We're *plugging away* on the backlog.

ru: подключаться к, подключиться к; приобщаться к, приобщиться
separable: inseparable — *plug into the network*, *plug into it*.
gloss: To connect to a system, a network, or a source of information.
examples: The sensor *plugs into* any USB port.
She *plugged into* the local music scene within a month.
We're *plugging into* the same data feed the newsroom uses.
